title: Bill Cosby Faces Possible Arrest Warrant After Accuser Says He Refused to Pay $59.25 Million Judgment and Disclose Finances
text:

 News Finance More Mail Search the web Advertisement Advertisement Return to Homepage Bill Cosby Faces Possible Arrest Warrant After Accuser Says He Refused to Pay $59.25 Million Judgment and Disclose Finances
 Taylor Camp Tue, November 10, 2026 at 2:25 a.m. UTC 3 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Bill Cosby 's accuser is asking a judge to hold him in contempt, and potentially jail him, for allegedly refusing to pay a massive $59.25 million civil judgment.
 The disgraced comedian, 89, is facing a new legal battle after Donna Motsinger requested Cosby be held in contempt of court, alleging he has ignored orders to disclose his finances and pay court-imposed sanctions.
 According to legal documents obtained by TMZ , Motsinger is also requesting an arrest warrant if Cosby fails to appear in court.
 Bill Cosby's Accuser Claims He Hasn't Paid $59.25 Million Judgment
 Donna Motsinger claims the comedian has not paid any portion of the $59.25 million civil judgment awarded to her. BY MEGA
 Motsinger alleges that Cosby has not paid any portion of the $59.25 million judgment awarded to her earlier this year.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement She also claims the former Cosby Show star has refused to provide information about his financial situation, including his bank accounts, income and assets.
 According to court documents, a judge ordered Cosby on October 9 to turn over the financial information and pay $1,560 in sanctions within 10 days.
 However, Motsinger alleges that he failed to comply with either requirement.
 Now, she wants the court to take additional action to force the comedian to cooperate.
 Bill Cosby Could Face Arrest and Jail Time
 Bill Cosby was ordered to disclose information about his bank accounts, income and assets, according to court documents. BY MEGA
 Motsinger is asking a judge to hold Cosby in contempt for allegedly disregarding the court's order.
 She is also requesting that an arrest warrant be issued if he fails to appear at a hearing.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement In addition to the potential warrant, Motsinger is seeking fines of up to $1,000 and five days in jail for each alleged violation.
 She also wants Cosby to pay $3,284 in attorney's fees and related costs.
 His attorney, Jennifer Bonjean , has previously described the 89-year-old as homebound and in poor health, and his legal team cited his blindness and limited mobility when he missed a deposition.
 After the verdict in March, Bonjean said Cosby "was denied a fair trial," adding, "No one can meaningfully defend against allegations that are a half-century old."
 The accuser is requesting that Cosby remain in custody until he complies with the court's order if he is found in contempt and continues refusing to cooperate.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement However, no arrest warrant has been issued in connection with the latest request.
 Bill Cosby Was Ordered to Pay Millions in Sexual Assault Case
 A jury found Bill Cosby liable in March 2026 in a civil case involving allegations of sexual assault dating back to 1972. BY MEGA
 The latest legal dispute stems from a civil lawsuit involving allegations dating back more than five decades.
 Motsinger accused Cosby of drugging and sexually assaulting her in 1972.
 In March 2026, a jury found the comedian liable and awarded Motsinger $19.25 million in damages.
 The jury subsequently added another $40 million in punitive damages, bringing the total judgment to $59.25 million.
 Cosby attempted to challenge the verdict and requested a new trial.
 However, a judge rejected his efforts in May.
 The former television star appealed the rulings to a higher court, and that appeal remains pending.
 Bill Cosby Faces Another Court Hearing in January
 A hearing on Donna Motsinger's request to hold Bill Cosby in contempt is scheduled for January 2027. BY MEGA
 Cosby's latest legal troubles come years after his release from prison following the overturning of his criminal sexual assault conviction.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The comedian was convicted in 2018 in a separate case involving Andrea Constand and served nearly three years behind bars .
 However, the Pennsylvania Supreme Court overturned his conviction in 2021 after determining that an earlier prosecutorial agreement had been violated.
 Cosby has consistently denied allegations of nonconsensual sexual activity.
 His latest legal dispute centers on whether he has complied with court orders related to Motsinger's civil judgment.
 A hearing on her contempt request is scheduled for January 2027.
